slides.title: Building Context Managers using Dunder Methods
slides.prompt: You can turn any class into a context manager by implementing the `__enter__()` and `__exit__()` magic methods. `__enter__` sets up the resource, while `__exit__` handles cleanup and optional exception suppression.

slides.title: The Setup Dunder Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method executed when entering the runtime context of a `with` statement.

slides.title: __exit__ Method Signature Parameters
slides.prompt: How many arguments (excluding `self`) must the `__exit__()` method accept to handle exceptions properly?

slides.title: The Teardown Dunder Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method executed when exiting the runtime context.

slides.title: Exception Suppression in __exit__
slides.prompt: How can an `__exit__()` method suppress an exception raised inside a `with` block so it doesn't propagate?

slides.title: __enter__ Return Value Usage
slides.prompt: Fill in the value bound to `res` in `with ManagedResource() as res:`.

slides.title: Normal Execution Exit Arguments
slides.prompt: If NO exception occurs inside a `with` block, what values are passed for `exc_type`, `exc_val`, and `exc_tb` into `__exit__`?
options: All three parameters are passed as None
They are set to empty string values
slides.correctAnswer: All three parameters are passed as None
